changes.old: “Very well,” I said shortly; “under the circumstances, quite as well as if I were either your real sister, or a man and a clergyman like yourself.”
changes.new: “We can be together very well,” I said shortly; “under the circumstances, quite as well as if I were either your real sister, or a man and a clergyman like yourself.”
changes.reason: Demonstrated misreading. A bare “Very well” reads today as reluctant assent; in context it is Jane's elliptical answer to St. John's “How can we be forever together … and unwed?” (“we can be together very well”), which the following “quite as well as if” depends on. Two of three blind readers misread it; the fresh reader of the corrected text read it correctly. Supplies only the elided predicate; keeps Brontë's “very well” so the rise to “perfectly well” at the next Jane line is preserved.
